title: The fixture's lineage is hand-drawn where the kernel resolves record pointers
body:
## Summary
Every fixture detail's lineage differs from the kernel's over the same items: the fixture draws run, style, project and hunt nodes itself and labels the self node by its kind, while the kernel resolves only the record's lineage pointers and labels self by the title.

## Description
app/(studio)/library/_port/fixtureCorpus.ts builds each record's lineage as display nodes (runNode, projNodes, style nodes, self(b.id, kind)) while raw.lineage stays [] except for derived items, so app/(studio)/library/_port/fixture.ts fixtureDetail returns those nodes verbatim. packages/kernel/src/library/detail.ts lineageOf resolves item.lineage pointers (library-item, run, job, candidate, style, project) by ROLE, BEFORE_SELF order and a title lookup, adds the plate lesson / doc bundle / audio group facet steps, and labels self with item.title. Fixed: the corpus writes its steps as raw.lineage pointers (run, style, project) and the fixture resolves them by the kernel's rule - best by exporting a pure half of lineageOf (item + titleOf) from the kernel so both sides call one function (demo-data-plane: one-interface-many-planes). The Lineage panel the screen draws would then show on the fixture exactly what the real side can show.

## Flow
- open /library?sel=image-0001 under GRAVITONE_PRODUCE_SIDE=fixture: 'this: image' plus two style doors
- the same item through the kernel: 'this: Wish list · frame 8622' and no style doors (no pointer)
- fix: pointers in raw.lineage, one resolver; extend the parity file's detail block to compare lineage

## Expected impact
The Library's lineage panel is designed against nodes the real side never draws (and never against what it does). Could break: library.live.spec lineage assertions written against the fixture's hand-drawn nodes, and the kit specimen.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - fixture/real parity of the detail's lineage
Before: lineage differs on 9/9 kinds (image 40/40, plate 40/40, style 9/9, motion 40/40, audio 40/40, video 40/40, doc 40/40, model 4/4, character 6/6) - measured this round with the parity harness
After: predicted 0/9 under a resolver shared with the kernel
Method: probe - Before measured on both sides; After not built: the shared resolver lives in packages/kernel (outside this round's paths) and the corpus rewrite is M
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:

app/(studio)/library/_port/fixtureCorpus.ts:139 base(): lineage: []
packages/kernel/src/library/detail.ts:38 function lineageOf(r: Reader, item: LibraryItem)
packages/kernel/src/library/detail.ts:55 const self = { role: "this", ref: { kind: "self", id: item.id }, label: item.title }

title: The fixture's media facts are drawn per item, though a blob has one set of facts
body:
## Summary
The fixture corpus draws media facts (mean luma, near-black, probe time) per ITEM, so one public file named by many items carries different facts on each; the kernel's media_facts are per blob sha.

## Description
app/(studio)/library/_port/fixtureCorpus.ts facts() draws meanLuma from the stream for every record, and a 'dark' plate overrides meanLuma 9 / nearBlack true on a blob it shares with bright plates (since 56d9e420 a plate's blob is its style's preset, so five shas carry ~1,950 plates' facts). packages/kernel/src/library/write.ts putMediaFacts keys facts by sha; detail.ts readFacts reads them per blob; the cover's nearBlack follows the blob. The fixture is self-inconsistent (demo-data-plane: fixture-self-consistency): the same picture is near-black on one tile and bright on the next. Fixed: facts memoised per sha in the corpus (the stream still drawn, so records are unchanged), and the near-black and unreadable cases given blobs of their own (e.g. a distinct url per case) so the attention story survives. Needs a choice of which blob carries the dark case - a fixture-design decision, hence B.

## Flow
- build the corpus; group records by raw.media.sha256
- the same sha shows several meanLuma values and both nearBlack states
- the kernel loaded with the same corpus answers one facts row per sha

## Expected impact
The detail's luma line and the near-black cover rule are shown against facts no store could hold. Could break: specs that pick 'a near-black plate' from the fixture.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - fixture self-consistency (one blob, one set of facts)
Before: detail.media differs from the kernel's (first fact per sha wins in the harness) on plate 40/40, image 19/40, motion 28/40, video 37/40, character 6/6
After: predicted 0 under per-sha facts
Method: probe - Before measured with the parity harness; After needs the dark-blob design choice, not built
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: tests/next-server/library-fixture-parity.test.ts: a 'media' case comparing fixtureDetail(id).media to libraryDetail(k.store, id).media over 40 items a kind (the harness loads one fact per sha); red on HEAD, green after
